title: Suspicious DNS Tunneling via High-Volume TXT Queries
description: Detects potential DNS tunneling by identifying hosts making excessive TXT record queries to external domains.

rule CobaltStrike_Shellcode_Rundll32 {
    meta:
        description = "Detects memory patterns associated with Cobalt Strike shellcode execution via rundll32"
        author = "SOC_Team"
        malpedia_reference = "https://malpedia.caad.fkie.fraunhofer.de/details/win.cobalt_strike"
        severity = 1
    strings:
        $a = { 6A 01 68 [2] 00 00 68 [2] 00 00 E8 [4] 83 C4 0C } // Common API call stack setup
        $b = "ReflectiveLoader" fullword ascii
        $c = { FF E0 } // JMP EAX often seen post-injection
    condition:
        all of them
}

arguments.summary: Data exfiltration incident involving DNS tunneling from compromised host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) to external C2 server at c2.evil-example.com. Over 2.3 GB of sensitive data, including PII and financial records, was exfiltrated via TXT record queries. The initial compromise occurred through a malicious rundll32 execution from the Temp directory, leading to Cobalt Strike beaconing and lateral movement via SMB. Containment actions included blocking the C2 IP (10.0.5.14) and isolating the host. Credential reset and endpoint hardening were performed during eradication.

Investigation revealed that the source host was compromised with Cobalt Strike beaconing to a known C2 server (198.51.100.23:443).
